string.text: Smart Steward: the autonomous steward failed - see smart_steward.log.
Food you gave no price in the Prices tab uses its average price as the base. Default: on.
Pack animals and riding horses you gave no price use their average price as the base. Default: on.
War and noble horses you gave no price use their average price as the base. When off, they are bought only under the upgrade horse price cap until you type a price. Default: off.
Open the Party Steward window when your party enters a town. Default: on.
Open the Party Steward window when your party enters a village. Default: on.

While the full-autonomous steward is on, it never takes your purse below this - both floors above rise to it when they are lower. Raise the price limits to let it spend more freely, never this. Default: 100,000. Range: 0 to 10,000,000.

For when you are rich and done with micromanaging: on arriving at a town or village the steward carries out its plan at once - no window, no questions, no warning - and sums it up in the message log. It never hires in the tavern and never takes your purse below Keep while autonomous. The Party Steward menu entry stays, to look or adjust. When off, the steward only proposes and you click. Default: off.
Max buy price = the item's base price (Prices tab) times this. 1.2 pays up to 20% over the average. Richer now? Raise it. Default: 1.2. Range: 0.1 to 10.0.
In a town of your kingdom that is not your clan's, send prisoners to its dungeon for influence instead of gold. Those that do not fit are ransomed. Default: off.
Count your prisoners when working out the food target - half a man each, as the game feeds them. Default: on.
Buy food up to the target and sell what is far above it. Default: on.
Food units kept for every man. A man eats about one unit in 20 days, so 2 lasts about 40 days. Default: 2.0. Range: 0.1 to 10.0.
Balanced buys the kinds you hold least of first - every different food lifts morale. Cheapest always buys the cheapest kind. Default: Balanced (variety first).
How far above the target food may pile up before the steward sells: 25 sells only above 125% of the target. Default: 25. Range: 0 to 500.
No purchase takes your purse below this many denars. Default: 1,000. Range: 0 to 1,000,000.
No horse, mule or camel purchase takes your purse below this. Food only answers to the floor above - food comes first. Default: 5,000. Range: 0 to 1,000,000.
Master switch. When off, the steward stays out of the way: no window, no menu entry, no warnings, nothing done on its own. Default: on.
Never pay more than this for a footman's horse, whatever the price book says. 0 = no cap. Not scaled by the buy multiplier. Default: 500. Range: 0 to 100,000.
Buy horses for the men who walk, so the party moves faster. Default: on.
Riding horses kept for every 100 men on foot: 110 is one each plus 10% spare. Default: 110. Range: 0 to 300.
Never pay more than this for one pack animal, whatever the price book says. 0 = no cap. Not scaled by the buy multiplier. Default: 300. Range: 0 to 100,000.
Keep a set number of pack animals (sumpter horses, mules, pack camels). Each one carries about 100 more weight. Default: on.
How many pack animals the party keeps. Default: 10. Range: 0 to 500.
Open the window by itself only when the steward has something to suggest. Default: on.
Troop ids the steward never ransoms or donates - the ones unticked in the Instructions tab's Prisoners to ransom list. Example: [ "looter", "sea_raiders_boss" ] Default: empty.
Also ransom (or donate) captured lords. A ransomed lord goes free. Default: off.
Offer your prisoners to the town's ransom broker. Default: on.
Sell food above the target plus the tolerance below, back down to the target, most-held kind first. Default: on.
Offer to sell captured gear in groups (armour, melee weapons, ranged, shields). Default: off.
Include weapons, armour, shields and ammunition in the loot sale. Default: on.
Never sell a piece worth more than this many denars. 0 = no cap. Pieces you locked in the inventory are never sold anyway. Default: 0. Range: 0 to 1,000,000.

Which pieces go first when the market cannot pay for everything: the cheapest (the most weight for the gold), the lowest price per kg, or the most expensive (the game's own habit). Default: Cheapest first.
Sell riding horses above the target, the dearest first. Default: on.
Sell pack animals above the target, the dearest first. Default: on.
Min sell price = the item's base price (Prices tab) times this. 0.8 sells at 80% of the average sell price or better; 0 sells at any price. Default: 0.8. Range: 0.0 to 10.0.
Sell upgrade horses above what your troops need, the dearest first. Default: on.
List the mercenary band in the town's tavern. Default: on.
Show the tavern section in towns: wanderers and mercenaries to hire with a click. Default: on.
List the wanderers for hire in the town's tavern. Default: on.
Never pay more than this for one upgrade horse, whatever the price book says. 0 = no cap. Not scaled by the buy multiplier. Default: 2,000. Range: 0 to 100,000.
Horses kept for troop upgrades also count as riding horses for the footmen until the upgrade takes them. Default: on.
Keep the horses your troops need to upgrade into cavalry. Default: on.
Extra horses on top of the automatic count, for each kind your troops upgrade into. Default: 0. Range: 0 to 100.
-1 keeps as many as your troops can use for upgrades right now. 0 or more keeps exactly that many of each kind your troops need. Default: -1. Range: -1 to 500.
Ask before you leave a town or village whose suggestions you never looked at. Default: on.
Your steward has suggestions you haven't looked at.
Average prices for pack animals and horses
Everything on offer is already in the plan.
Everything that may go is already in the plan. Locked ones never are.
Your clan's companion limit is reached.

The market has no gold left to pay for more.
The next one would fetch less than its min sell price - a town's prices fall as you sell.
Nothing on offer the steward may buy: none in the market, unticked in the Prices tab, or dearer than its max buy price.
Nothing to sell: none held, all locked, or unticked for selling in the Prices tab.
What is left is already planned for another row.
The next one costs more than its max buy price - a town's prices climb as you buy.
Only ever sold, ransomed or donated - never bought.
Steward: nothing was done - see smart_steward.log.
Nothing for the steward to do here.
Show the kinds of animal in this row
Smart Steward: something went wrong - the window closed. See smart_steward.log.
Your standing orders to the steward. Changes are saved at once - to settings.json, and Mod Options shows them too. Hover a name for what it does.
Smart Steward: nothing to plan here ({WHY}).
Smart Steward: the window could not open - see smart_steward.log.
Final = your base price × the multiplier. An empty box uses the grey average price where auto-fill is on (Instructions tab, Prices). Unticked items are never bought or sold.
Clear your prices - the grey average applies again
Ticked: the steward may ransom (or donate) this troop.
Click ±1 · Shift ±5 · Ctrl all · names in gold open the Encyclopedia
You cannot afford this deal - take something back.
The market cannot pay for all the sales.
